question: What physical appearance defines congenital talipes equinovarus in a newborn?

options.A: The toes are permanently spread wide apart
options.B: The heel bone is completely missing at birth
options.C: The foot is twisted inward and downward
options.D: The foot is pointed straight upward and flat

explanation: Clubfoot physically pulls the foot in these specific directions due to tight tendons and ligaments. [learn more](BMP220_U2_T6#BMP220_U2_T6_h1)

question: How does postural clubfoot differ from true congenital clubfoot?

options.A: Postural clubfoot requires immediate surgical intervention at birth
options.B: Postural clubfoot involves missing bones in the lower leg
options.C: Postural clubfoot is flexible and corrects easily with gentle stretching
options.D: Postural clubfoot only happens in premature male infants

explanation: True congenital clubfoot is rigid and cannot be easily pushed into a normal position by hand, unlike flexible postural variations. [learn more](BMP220_U2_T6#BMP220_U2_T6_h1)

question: Which term describes the high arch commonly seen in the midfoot of a clubfoot?
explanation: Cavus specifically refers to the accentuated high arch component of the structural deformity. [learn more](BMP220_U2_T6#BMP220_U2_T6_h2)

question: Which of the following is NOT a feature evaluated during a physical assessment of clubfoot?

options.A: Presence of webbed toes on the affected foot
options.B: Size of the calf muscle on the lower leg
options.C: Rigidity and flexibility of the ankle joint
options.D: Tilt and position of the newborn heel

explanation: Webbed toes syndactyly is a different anomaly and is not a defining characteristic of talipes equinovarus. [learn more](BMP220_U2_T6#BMP220_U2_T6_h2)

question: Why should midwives avoid applying tight improvised bandages to a newborn with clubfoot?

options.A: It prevents the mother from breastfeeding successfully
options.B: It permanently fuses the bones in the wrong position
options.C: It can damage fragile skin and restrict blood circulation
options.D: It speeds up bone growth too quickly in the joint

explanation: Newborn skin is very delicate, and tight wrapping risks causing pressure sores or cutting off blood supply. [learn more](BMP220_U2_T6#BMP220_U2_T6_h3)

question: What is the primary immediate psychological need of parents upon discovering a birth defect like clubfoot?

options.A: Detailed instruction on how to perform surgical procedures
options.B: Strict isolation from other new mothers in the ward
options.C: Compassionate reassurance that the condition is correctable
options.D: Immediate referral for genetic counseling and DNA testing

explanation: Parents benefit most from knowing early on that modern treatment has a very high success rate for clubfoot. [learn more](BMP220_U2_T6#BMP220_U2_T6_h3)

question: What is the name of the widely accepted serial casting method used to treat clubfoot?
explanation: The Ponseti method uses gentle manipulation and weekly casting to correct clubfoot deformity without major early surgery. [learn more](BMP220_U2_T6#BMP220_U2_T6_h4)

question: A mother brings a two-week-old infant with clubfoot to the clinic. What is the most appropriate action for the midwife?

options.A: Wait until the child is walking before taking any clinical action
options.B: Prescribe heavy oral pain relievers to relax the newborn leg
options.C: Arrange a prompt referral to a specialized pediatric orthopedic clinic
options.D: Apply a rigid plaster cast immediately in the primary clinic room

explanation: Early specialist referral ensures treatment starts while the tissues are supple and responsive to serial casting. [learn more](BMP220_U2_T6#BMP220_U2_T6_h4)

question: What device is worn after serial casting to prevent clubfoot from relapsing?
explanation: The foot abduction brace keeps the feet turned outward to maintain the correction achieved during casting. [learn more](BMP220_U2_T6#BMP220_U2_T6_h5)

question: Why is long-term compliance with brace-wearing crucial after clubfoot casting is finished?

options.A: It prevents the child from developing rashes from the cast
options.B: Clubfoot has a high natural tendency to relapse without ongoing support
options.C: The brace helps the leg bones grow longer and stronger
options.D: It allows the baby to learn how to crawl much faster

explanation: Without consistent bracing during early childhood, the tight tendons can pull the foot back into the clubfoot position. [learn more](BMP220_U2_T6#BMP220_U2_T6_h5)
